messages:
maria: Quick thread — Customer FwdLabs asked for a firm checklist before we recommend quantization and batching in prod. They want eval-triggered alerts wired to their SREs. Can we agree acceptance gates?

alex: High level: we need (1) perf SLOs (p99 < 250ms for short chats), (2) quality regression threshold on eval suite, (3) clear rollback policy + canary.

joni: +1. Also add cost guardrails: recommended quant/profile should not degrade per-conversation cost more than 15% relative to their baseline unless quality is improved.

sam: On eval-alerts — do we require customer to provide label sets, or ship with our generic prompt suites? FwdLabs wants both.

lina: We should offer baseline public eval sets for quick onboarding and let them attach private sets for stricter gating. Product-bot: New action: create pilot onboarding template.

maria: For rollout plan proposal: Phase 0 = advisory (dry-run recommendations only). Phase 1 = opt-in canary (1% traffic + manual review). Phase 2 = automated rollout with eval-triggered guardrails. Any objections?

alex: Sounds reasonable. Need precise metrics for "manual review": review window 24h, checklist includes human spot-check on 200 samples, automatic diff on embedding drift > 0.08.

joni: Regarding quantization profiles: we must enumerate compatible model families and accuracy regressions per profile. Recommend we only auto-suggest INT8 for transformers with FP32->INT8 delta < 2% on top-1 token loss across cust evals.

sam: Implementation note for runtime team: kv-cache interaction when using quantized kernels can spike memory a bit — call that out in docs and our canary checklist.

maria: Acceptance gate draft (single-line list to include in pilot docs):
- Performance: p50/p95/p99 targets, sample throughput >= X TPS
- Quality: eval delta within threshold, no production-feedback regressions > 1%
- Safety: no new high-severity safety hits in evals
- Observability: audit log + eval-alerts wired to webhook
- Rollback: automatic fallback to previous model/variant on alert

lina: We should include an economics view: estimated token cost delta and expected savings from batching (offset quantization cost). Maybe add a field: expected tokens/sec uplift.

alex: For eval-triggered alerts format, propose this webhook payload (minimal):
```json
{
  "alert_id": "uuid",
  "model": "model-name",
  "metric": "eval_concordance",
  "delta": -0.03,
  "threshold": -0.02,
  "samples_url": "https://redwood.example/alerts/uuid/samples"
}
```

maria: Good. Joni, can you estimate how many cust-specific eval runs we need to be confident? (ballpark)

joni: Ballpark: 10k prompt-response pairs to hit stable estimates across common tasks, but initial gating can use 1k with higher confidence intervals and human review.

sam: Ops question — who owns the webhook delivery SLA for eval-alerts? product or eng-runtime?

lina: Runtime owns delivery and retries, product owns schema and UX. Add it to the pilot RACI.

maria: Action items:
- joni: draft quant acceptance criteria doc + sample numbers (due EOD Thu)
- alex: formalize canary checklist and manual review steps (due Mon)
- sam: add runtime caveats and memory note to docs (due Fri)
- lina: create econ estimate template for pilot customers (due Fri)

product-bot: Created task list: /tasks create "Optimize pilot: FwdLabs gating" assigned to joni,alex,sam,lina due 2026-04-09

maria: If nobody objects, I'll present this as the pilot proposal in next week's PM sync. Quick thumbs? :thumbsup:

alex: :thumbsup:

joni: :thumbsup:
